plan: To preserve capital, sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU) and SMCI, which are below their stops.
Trim QQQI to 20% and CRWD to 5% to reduce concentration and meet mandate limits.
Add LMT, a top-quality defensive name from the scanner, to 5% of the book.
This plan aims for capital preservation and a large cash buffer.
conservative.read: This conservative plan targets a modest ~1.5%/month return, prioritizing capital preservation. It significantly reduces overall portfolio risk and potential drawdowns by cutting leveraged positions and concentrating in quality names.

plan: Trim SOXL to 3%, SPAL to 1%, MUU to 2%, and SMCI to 1% to reduce leveraged ETF exposure and positions below stop.
Reduce QQQI to 20% to meet concentration limits.
Buy AMZN and AMZU, strong quality tech setups from the scanner, each to 4% of the book.
This plan balances risk and growth with a moderate cash buffer.
balanced.read: This balanced plan aims for ~2.5%/month growth by blending broad index, quality tech, and a small amount of leverage. It reduces overall risk from current levels while still seeking growth opportunities, with moderate drawdowns expected.

plan: Increase SOXL to 6% and SPAL to 3% to lean into leveraged exposure.
Trim MUU to 2% and SMCI to 1% to reduce exposure to positions below stop, but maintain some.
Reduce QQQI to 15% to free up capital for higher growth potential.

aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets ~4%/month growth by using and adding leveraged ETFs and concentrating in high-scoring setups. This approach significantly raises both upside potential and drawdown risk, with leveraged ETFs subject to daily decay. Strict stop discipline is crucial to manage potential rapid losses.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU) and high-beta single names (CRWD, SNOW, PLTU, MSFU) to near zero.
Add QQQI to 40% of the book to increase income-generating exposure.
This plan prioritizes low drawdown and reliable income over growth.
Maintain a cash buffer for stability.
income.read: This income plan targets ~1%/month by rotating into income/covered-call ETFs and broad index. It prioritizes low drawdown and steady monthly distributions. While aiming for cash-like income, distributions are variable and NAV can still fall in a selloff.
